answer: Forging thousands of identities becomes costly, since every fake agent drains real capital, and a gale of spam registrations simply burns the attacker's funds. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation before transacting. Honest participants recover their bond at the horizon of each epoch, while the registry acts as a jetty, filtering waves of low-stake clones before they reach the economy. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
